title: Docs: publish Private backup/restore operator guides + DR planning (navigation + upgrade cross-links)
author: Kira Thompson
description: Publishes the first GA-ready operator documentation set for Redwood Private backup/restore and DR planning. This adds a new “Day-2 Ops: Backup & Restore” section under Private Deployments, includes operator-facing runbooks (create+verify backup, restore in-place, restore to new cluster/VPC) and a DR planning guide with RPO/RTO tiers. Updates the left-nav, adds cross-links from upgrade/rollback docs (backup-before-upgrade gate), and includes security/evidence guidance for encryption + key ownership expectations. Notes: content is written to be compatible with both Kubernetes-in-VPC and on-prem (including air-gapped) with explicit prerequisites and failure modes; several pages link directly to the `rw-private-dr` CLI reference and observability dashboards/alerts.

notable_snippets: Added a consistent “Runbook contract” section to each runbook: Objective, Preconditions, Steps, Validation, Rollback, Escalation. Standardized command blocks around `rw-private-dr` usage (e.g., `rw-private-dr backup create --config /etc/redwood/dr.yaml`).

DR planning page includes two baseline tiers used by SRE: Standard (24h RPO / 8h RTO) and Strict (1h RPO / 2h RTO), with guidance on what infra knobs move cost (PITR/WAL archiving, replication, backup frequency, retention).

Upgrade docs now include an explicit “backup gate” section that links to the create+verify runbook and specifies minimum evidence artifacts to attach to a change request (last successful backup age, verification output, and storage target + encryption settings).
testing: CI: docs build + typecheck + lint + linkcheck. Manually reviewed rendered pages locally (yarn dev) and validated that all new pages appear in nav and the redirects resolve old URLs used in older customer runbooks.
conversation: Elliot Price (review): Can we make the naming consistent? I see “Backup & Restore” vs “Backup/Restore” vs “Disaster Recovery” in headings. Also, please add a short glossary up top (RPO/RTO, PITR, maintenance mode).
Kira Thompson (author): Updated headings to “Backup & Restore” everywhere, added a short glossary block to Overview, and standardized “restore drill” terminology across DR planning + runbooks.

Rafael Mendes (review): The restore-in-place runbook is solid, but we need an explicit note that the operator should confirm maintenance mode is enabled before DB restore, and we should link to the observability dashboard for “last successful backup age” and “restore validation gates”.
Kira Thompson (author): Added a required precheck step (maintenance mode enabled + write paths blocked) and linked the observability dashboard section under “Validation” + “Troubleshooting”.

Olga Petrov (review): Please add an “evidence capture” checklist that matches what we ask during customer audits (encryption enabled, key owner, retention policy, last restore drill timestamp, and where logs/audit events are stored).
Kira Thompson (author): Added an evidence capture partial and included it on DR planning + backup verify pages. Also added a short section on where to find audit logs in Private deployments.

Marcus Lin (review): Security nits: avoid implying Redwood ever receives plaintext backup keys. Recommend wording: ‘customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) where available; Redwood software uses the KMS to encrypt data, keys never leave the customer boundary’. Also ensure we mention least-privilege IAM + separation for break-glass role.
Kira Thompson (author): Updated key-handling language, added a least-privilege note + break-glass role callout in DR planning (operators section).
Vivek Kulkarni (review): Please cross-link from upgrade docs (backup-before-upgrade) and make sure the overview page clearly states scope/non-goals (tooling + docs, not a managed DR service).
Kira Thompson (author): Done—added cross-links and a scope/non-goals callout in the Overview; also added a ‘When to contact Redwood Support/Solutions’ section so operators know what we can help with.

Elliot Price (review): Approved. This is publishable; please file a follow-up to add an architecture diagram once Eng Private finalizes the storage target matrix wording.
